text.content:
Tatzlford is under a supernatural storm. Three level 13 manifestations anchor it, and a deliberately weakened level 16 complex hazard represents the storm itself tearing at the town. Built for a level 15 party. Treat it as more dangerous than the creature XP suggests: the settlement objectives eat actions and split the party.

The cast

  • @UUID[Compendium.tatzleford-tempest.actors.Actor.QueensTempstmt07]{Queen's Tempest} — Hazard 16, complex. Its own initiative entry. Rolls the routine each turn.
  • @UUID[Compendium.tatzleford-tempest.actors.Actor.TempestVortxMTah]{Vortex Tempest} — Creature 13, HP 245. Central streets, chokepoints, pulls enemies in.
  • @UUID[Compendium.tatzleford-tempest.actors.Actor.TempestLghtnPWdk]{Lightning Tempest} — Creature 13, HP 205. Fights at range, relocates after attacking.
  • @UUID[Compendium.tatzleford-tempest.actors.Actor.TempestDelugZgnu]{Deluge Tempest} — Creature 13, HP 225. Owns the river, the bridge, and low ground.

The hazard and the three creatures roll separate initiative.

Before the first round

  1. Open the scene. @UUID[Compendium.tatzleford-tempest.scenes.Scene.TempestTatzlfrd1]{The Queen's Tempest at Tatzlford}. The three Tempests are already placed. The map art comes from the premium pf2e-kingmaker module; without it the scene renders black, so install Kingmaker before you run this.
  2. Paint the district grid. Open the Tempest tools in the scene controls (GM only) and drag-paint the town core. Left-drag paints a cell, right-drag erases. Painted cells are the storm's whole world: routines, random sector rolls, and every storm movement stay inside them. Cover the town from Tatzlford Lodge in the west to Ironhand Smithy in the east, plus the bridge and the river bank. Roughly 45–55 cells; it takes under a minute.
  3. Cell size is frozen at first paint. The default cell is 12 squares — 60 ft, exactly the Thunderclap burst. Change the world setting before you paint if you want coarser or finer districts; changing it afterwards invalidates the painted cells.
  4. Open the storm console. @UUID[Compendium.tatzleford-tempest.macros.Macro.TempestMacroCnsl]{Open the Storm Console}, or the console button in the Tempest tool group. Everything below runs from there.
  5. Decide what is at stake. Where are the civilians, the escape routes, the things the party will regret losing? Name them before round one so the collateral markers land on something the players already care about.

What the module does and does not do

The overlay tracks state and shows it to the players. It never rolls a save, applies damage, moves a creature, or resolves a condition — you resolve everything through PF2e's normal cards. Toggling a cell to Damaged or Destroyed is a deliberate GM act.

At the beginning of each @UUID[Compendium.tatzleford-tempest.actors.Actor.QueensTempstmt07]{Queen's Tempest} turn:

  1. Resolve last turn's collateral. Every marker placed on the previous hazard turn resolves now, unless a hero prevented it or its Tempest died first. Each unresolved marker deals 1 damage hit to its cell or landmark — toggle it on the overlay.
  2. Press Take the Hazard Turn in the console. One click rolls 1d3 for the anchor, rolls a random painted sector, draws that routine's template over it, and whispers you one card carrying the area, the save, and the damage.
  3. If that Tempest is dead, the button stops there and says so: describe the clouds trying to produce the effect and faltering. The storm takes no action this round. Do not reroll.
  4. Resolve the creature-facing effect from the card's links. The template is scaled to fill the whole district so the table can see what is hit; the card quotes the rule's real area, and that is the area you resolve against.
  5. Place the collateral marker and say out loud what is about to be lost. "The bridge is going" beats "sector 4 takes a hit."

1 — Thunderclap

@Template[burst|distance:30] within the selected sector. A concussive peal.

  • Critical Success No effect.
  • Success Half damage.
  • Failure @Damage[8d10[sonic]] damage, deafened for 1 round, pushed 10 feet from the center.
  • Critical Failure Double damage, deafened for 1 minute, pushed 20 feet, and knocked prone.

Collateral Windows shatter, doors burst, roofs and masonry come down.

2 — Queen's Lightning

One creature in the selected sector. If nobody is there, the bolt takes a prominent structure and only the collateral is created.

  • Critical Success No damage.
  • Success Half damage.
  • Failure @Damage[10d8[electricity]] damage.
  • Critical Failure Double damage plus @Damage[2d6[persistent,electricity]].

Collateral Supernatural fire takes hold in the rain.

3 — Rending Deluge

@Template[cone|distance:30] from an edge or watercourse in the selected sector. Rain, floodwater, and debris.

  • Critical Success No damage.
  • Success Half damage.
  • Failure @Damage[6d10[bludgeoning]] damage and pushed 20 feet from the cone's origin.
  • Critical Failure Double damage, hurled 30 feet, and knocked prone.

Collateral Floodwater uproots trees, strips roofs, sweeps away carts and walls.

Then the Tempests act

On their own initiative entries, as ordinary creatures. Move the storm overlay when you commit an advance from the console; that is cosmetic weather, separate from where the three creatures stand.

A creature that can affect a threatened sector spends 2 actions and attempts a skill check against DC 35. It does not need to stand in the sector if its method plausibly reaches that far. Drop the DC to 33 when the approach is particularly suitable and raise it to 37 when it is a stretch.

Click the skill the player chose: @Check[arcana|dc:35|name:Storm Intervention] · @Check[nature|dc:35|name:Storm Intervention] · @Check[athletics|dc:35|name:Storm Intervention] · @Check[acrobatics|dc:35|name:Storm Intervention] · @Check[crafting|dc:35|name:Storm Intervention] · @Check[survival|dc:35|name:Storm Intervention]

Approaches

  • Arcana or Nature — disrupt the supernatural weather.
  • Athletics — brace a structure, clear debris, divert water.
  • Acrobatics — cross a collapsing area, make a dangerous rescue.
  • Crafting — reinforce or repair a threatened structure.
  • Survival — predict and redirect wind or floodwater.
  • Any credible spell, class feature, or item, usually with a relevant check.

Degrees of success

  • Critical Success The collateral event is prevented and the intervention buys something extra: a Hero Point, a −1 circumstance penalty to the matching Tempest's AC until the end of its next turn, or a comparable benefit.
  • Success The collateral event is prevented.
  • Failure The collateral event resolves normally.
  • Critical Failure The collateral event resolves and the intervening creature suffers the rolled hazard effect as though it stood in the area. If it was already affected, use the worse result rather than applying the damage twice.

Let creative interventions work when they fit the fiction. The DC and the action cost exist for consistency; the real decision is whether a hero spends a turn containing the disaster instead of attacking a Tempest.

Every painted cell and every landmark sits in one of three states.

  • Safe — no significant storm damage.
  • Damaged — still usable, but a serious setback. Add difficult or uneven terrain, blocked routes, lost shelter, endangered civilians.
  • Destroyed — the landmark is unusable or the neighbourhood is devastated. Its loss should have a clear consequence after the encounter.

An unresolved collateral event deals 1 damage hit. The first hit moves a target from Safe to Damaged. When accumulated hits equal its durability, it becomes Destroyed. Hits in between worsen the fiction while the target stays Damaged.

The design doc's Temple and Mill have no counterpart on the Tatzlford map, so they are omitted. If you want them, nominate two of the ordinary landmarks as stand-ins and drop their durability to 2 in the console.

Toggling state on the map

Pick the damage tool in the Tempest scene-control group. Left-click a painted cell to cycle it Safe → Damaged → Destroyed; right-click steps it back. Damaged cells wash yellow, destroyed cells red, and the change reaches every connected player the moment you make it. The console carries the same tally plus the landmark hit pips.

Two world settings matter here: hide the whole overlay from players while you prepare, and set your own overlay opacity if the fills sit too heavy over the map.

Immediate map effects

When an area becomes Damaged or Destroyed, change the tactical map where it is cheap to do so: rubble, fire, floodwater, fallen trees, a blocked street. The point is to make the town's condition visible, not to invent a second rules layer. Do not track structural Hit Points.

These preferences guide movement only. The @UUID[Compendium.tatzleford-tempest.actors.Actor.QueensTempstmt07]{Queen's Tempest} always picks collateral sectors at random.

@UUID[Compendium.tatzleford-tempest.actors.Actor.TempestVortxMTah]{Vortex Tempest}

The Roar. HP 245. Starts on the ring road just west of Tatzlford Fort, in the central streets. It occupies chokepoints, drags enemies into reach with Draw the Sky, and punishes ranged attackers with Rolling Echo. It prefers tall, sturdy structures — the fort and the watchtowers. Its kit is sonic; a vortex is what thunder sounds like up close.

@UUID[Compendium.tatzleford-tempest.actors.Actor.TempestLghtnPWdk]{Lightning Tempest}

The Wrath. HP 205. Starts in the open ground between the bridge and the town's west approach, with clear lines to both. It stays at range, opens on clustered heroes with Forked Lightning, and teleports away with Ride the Bolt the moment anyone closes. It gravitates toward towers, metal, and crowds. Never let it get pinned in a street.

@UUID[Compendium.tatzleford-tempest.actors.Actor.TempestDelugZgnu]{Deluge Tempest}

The Flood. HP 225. Starts in the Skunk River just south of the bridge. It owns the crossing: Flash Flood down the length of the bridge, Undertow on anyone wading, Drown the Streets to make a whole sector cost double. Its job is to split the party across the river.

Moving across the map

Tatzlford is large. If ordinary movement makes interventions unviable, allow a creature to spend 2 actions to rush to an adjacent district cell — sprinting alleys, flying over roofs, cutting through buildings. Fast movement, teleportation, and the obvious spells reduce or bypass that cost at your discretion.

Destroying a Tempest

When a Tempest drops, its routine result is permanently suppressed and any unresolved collateral marker it created is removed. The console lights an indicator when a Tempest actor hits 0 HP; you still flip its destroyed toggle by hand, so a dying-but-not-dead creature does not switch the storm off early.

Ending the encounter

The last Tempest's death ends the @UUID[Compendium.tatzleford-tempest.actors.Actor.QueensTempstmt07]{Queen's Tempest} immediately. Clear every pending marker. The rain slackens and the clouds split. Then read the damage tracks out loud: surviving routes, ruined landmarks, rescued civilians, permanent scars. Those outcomes should matter in later scenes even if they impose no combat penalty.

• Hazard routine: roll 1d3, then a random painted cell.
  • A dead Tempest's result does nothing. Do not reroll.
  • A surviving result applies its effect now and creates collateral for the next hazard turn.
  • Intervention: 2 actions, DC 35 (33 suitable / 37 difficult).
  • Destroying a Tempest cancels its pending collateral and suppresses its future result.
  • Unresolved collateral deals 1 damage hit.
  • Durability: Skunk River Bridge 2, Tatzlford Fort 3, ordinary sector 3.
  • States: Safe → Damaged → Destroyed.
  • All three routine saves are DC 38. All Tempest ability saves are DC 35.
  • HP: Vortex 245, Deluge 225, Lightning 205. All three: AC 34, Fort +27, Ref +25, Will +22, Perception +25, fly 60 ft, physical resistance 10 except magical.
  • Default district cell: 12 squares = 60 ft, one Thunderclap burst.
